rows.description: A disabled or ill teenager may feel smothered when family decides everything for them out of love and fear. Involving them in decisions and allowing safe risks respects their growing autonomy.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: affection, admiration, fear, trust

rows.description: A young adult with disability meets stairs, rigid rules or people who talk to their companion instead of them. Recognising these as barriers in the world, not personal failings, guides fair and respectful action.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A person living long-term with illness or disability may feel grief over lost plans, frustration with limits and pride in their resilience, sometimes on the same day. All of these are valid and none is a failure of attitude.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: grief, anger, pride

rows.subtype: Partner, friend or employer supporting well [Response]
rows.description: A supportive person asks what help is wanted, adapts plans without fuss and never treats the person as inspirational or as a burden. Reliability and honest conversation matter more than grand gestures.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child with a fracture or bad fall may be scared, angry at being stopped from playing and worried about the future. Comfort, honest information and small achievable goals help the mind heal along with the body.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: anger, fear, anxiety, hurt

rows.description: A teenage sportsperson sidelined by injury may feel lost, low and afraid of being replaced. Staying part of the team, keeping other interests and following medical advice protect the mind and the recovery.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager eager to return may hide pain to play again, risking a worse injury. Understanding that healing has its own pace, and that a coach or parent will not think less of them, makes honesty easier.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult in recovery feels impatient, dependent on others and annoyed at the slow pace, and may swing between overdoing and giving up. Steady, measured progress is better than either extreme.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A person after a road accident or serious injury may feel jumpy, avoid the place or vehicle and replay the event. Time, support and, if fear lingers, professional help allow trust in the world to return.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A helper offers practical support, listens to frustration without hurrying the person's mood, celebrates small gains and lets them do what they can. They avoid taking over and avoid saying it could have been worse.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
